::: {.lead}
Today you use AI with PowerPoint, as in Lectures 3, 4, 17 and 18. There are
no new ideas: you get an outline from an AI tool, check it, make the
slides, and check an AI-made deck before a meeting. **Part A** is in the
apps; **Part B** is on a simulator of the interactive page: on paper, scan
its QR code; on the screen, click its link. After each step, write your
result in its box.
:::

## Before you start

- **You need:** a lab computer with PowerPoint, a browser and an AI
  assistant that the university allows (for example
  `copilot.microsoft.com`).
- **No lab computer today?** Do Part B of each experiment on your phone. Do
  Part A later on any computer with PowerPoint.
- **The story:** Huda, the office manager of Sunrise Company, gives a
  3-minute talk, *Going paperless*, to 12 office staff. Her notes: *we
  print 6,500 pages a month; the plan is shared folders and e-forms; our
  goal is half the paper in three months.*
- **Check:** the results are at the end of this worksheet. Look only after
  you try. On the interactive page, every step has a check that answers at
  once.

## Experiment 1 · An outline from an AI tool

**The idea (Lectures 3, 4 and 18):** AI writes likely words, so it can
invent a number or a source: you compare every number with your own notes.
A clear prompt has a task, a context and a format, and never names or phone
numbers. In Outline view, a line at the left edge is a slide; Tab makes a
point.

**Aim:** get Huda's outline from an AI tool, check it, and make the slides.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the apps (an AI assistant and PowerPoint)**
:::

1. Ask an AI tool: *Make an outline of 5 slides for a 3-minute talk to 12
   office staff about going paperless. Each slide: a title and 3 points of
   at most 8 words. Do not invent numbers or sources.* Mark every number
   and every source in the answer, and compare them with Huda's notes.

   {{< record "A number or a source that I corrected or deleted (or: none)" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   Every number must be from Huda's notes: **6,500** pages, half in
   **three** months. Delete a source that you cannot open. If the AI added
   no number and no source, write *none*.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   The AI writes "We print 9,000 pages a month". Huda's notes say 6,500.
   What do you do?

   - [x] Correct it from the notes.

     Why: The notes are the source; the AI may invent a number.

   - [ ] Keep it: the AI knows best.

     Why: The AI does not know Huda's office.

   - [ ] Write both numbers.

     Why: Only the true number goes on the slide.
   :::

2. Cut every point to 8 words or fewer. Paste the outline into a new
   presentation with **View › Outline** and fix the levels with **Tab** and
   **Shift + Tab**. Give slide 1 the layout **Title Slide**.

   {{< record "The five slide titles" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   A good outline: 1 *Going paperless* (Huda, Office Manager); 2 *The
   problem* (we print 6,500 pages a month); 3 *The plan* (shared folders,
   e-forms); 4 *Our goal* (half the paper in three months); 5 *Questions?*
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   The prompt says "12 office staff". Why not the names of the staff?

   - [x] Names are personal data, and the AI does not need them.

     Why: Never type personal data into an AI tool.

   - [ ] The AI cannot read names.

     Why: It can; the point is that names are personal data.

   - [ ] Names make the outline too long.

     Why: The reason is privacy, not length.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-09/sims/outline-lab.html" poster="../../week-09/sims/outline-lab.png" title="Outline Lab: from an AI outline to slides" >}}

3. In **Outline Lab**, do the four tasks for Huda's outline: the levels,
   the wrong number, the invented source and the long point. Which source
   did you delete?

   {{< record "The deleted source: …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   The made-up report (a source that no search finds): an invented source
   is a hallucination. The wrong number, 9,000, becomes 6,500.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Which layout fits the first slide, *Going paperless*?

   - [x] Title Slide

     Why: The first slide gives the topic and the speaker.

   - [ ] Two Content

     Why: Two Content puts two boxes side by side.

   - [ ] Blank

     Why: The first slide needs a title and the speaker's name.
   :::

## Experiment 2 · Ready for Monday?

**The idea (Lectures 17 and 18):** before the meeting, check each slide:
the numbers, the sources, the picture (no wrong letters), the prompt (no
personal data), the amount of text (3–5 short points) and a short note on
what the AI did.

**Aim:** finish Huda's deck, and check it slide by slide.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (PowerPoint)**
:::

1. In your deck, choose a theme. On slide 3, add a picture from **Insert ›
   Pictures › Stock Images** (search *folder*) with its alt text. Add a last
   slide with the note *Outline made with AI help and checked by Huda.*

   {{< record "My alt text … ; my note on the last slide …" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   A good alt text says what the picture shows, for example "Blue folders
   on a shelf". The note on the last slide tells the staff what the AI did.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   How does Huda tell the staff that AI helped?

   - [x] A short note: outline made with AI help and checked by her.

     Why: An honest note says what the AI did.

   - [ ] She says nothing.

     Why: Honest work says when AI was used.

   - [ ] She deletes every AI word.

     Why: The AI help is fine when she checks it and says so.
   :::

2. Press **F5** and check every slide with the checks: numbers, sources,
   picture, text and the note. Write one fix that you made.

   {{< record "One fix that I made" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   A good answer, for example: "I cut a point of 11 words", "I corrected
   9,000 to 6,500" or "I wrote alt text for the picture".
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   The slide *Our goal* has five long sentences. What is the fix?

   - [x] Keep 3–5 short points, and say the rest.

     Why: Few words on the slide; the details are what you say.

   - [ ] Make the font smaller.

     Why: Small text is hard to read from the back of the room.

   - [ ] Add a sixth sentence that sums up.

     Why: More text makes the problem bigger.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-10/sims/ai-deck-check.html" poster="../../week-10/sims/ai-deck-check.png" title="AI Deck Check: ready for Monday?" kind="game" >}}

3. Play **AI Deck Check**: for each of Huda's six slides, choose the best
   fix. What is the fix for the AI picture with "SUNRSIE CMOPANY" on a
   sign?

   {{< record "The fix for the picture: …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **A picture without text, and the name typed on the slide**: AI pictures
   often draw wrong letters.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   A prompt in Huda's notes has the names and phone numbers of the staff.
   What is the fix?

   - [x] Take the names and phone numbers out of the prompt.

     Why: Never type personal data into an AI tool.

   - [ ] Keep them: the AI writes better with names.

     Why: Personal data must stay private.

   - [ ] Write only the phone numbers.

     Why: Phone numbers are personal data too.
   :::
